Neuberg, Kherson, early 1800s. Joseph Sr Kiehlbauch [TG453802] was born 22 Jan 1826 in Neuberg, Cherson Province, in the New Odessa district of Russia, and Johanna Knoepfle [TG171824] was born 25 Jul 1824 in the nearby colony of Alexanderhilf, Grossliebental district. These were Black Sea German farming colonies near Odessa.. Your choices are: Walk to the Odessa road. Stay in the colony

Odessa, mid-1800s. Barbara Maier/Beck [TG513452] died 11 Jun 1856 in Odessa. Her daughter-in-law line continued through Constantin Beck [TG268612] (born 16 May 1812 in Wuerttemberg, Germany; died 4 Aug 1857 in Lustdorf, Odessa) and his wife, and through Barbara Beck [TG835097], born 22 Jan 1850 in Lustdorf, Russia. Many Russian Germans left for North America from the 1870s, embarking at Bremen or Hamburg.. Your choices are: Board the steamship at Bremen/Hamburg. Follow the wagon road north

Atlantic to New York, then rail west. Josef Kiehlbauch [TG274361], son of Joseph Sr and Johanna, was born 1 Jan 1850 in Neuberg, Russia. He married Barbara Beck, and their daughter Amelia was born later in South Dakota. Josef died 14 Sep 1908 in Chicago, Cook County, Illinois — a rail hub on the way west. The exact ship and manifest for this family have not been found, and are not claimed here.. Your choices are: Ride the rails to Chicago. Continue west to Dakota Territory

Tyndall, Bon Homme County, South Dakota. Joseph Sr Kiehlbauch died 29 May 1902 in Tyndall, Bon Homme County, South Dakota. Barbara Beck died there 15 Jul 1923. Their granddaughter Amelia Kiehlbauch [TG472690] was born in Tyndall on 12 Jan 1880 and died 29 Aug 1969 in Fresno, California. She married Burke C. Maynard [TG239670] — the link back to the branch you already explored. Black Sea German settlements in Bon Homme County included Avon, Scotland, and Tyndall.. Your choices are: Return toward the Maynard home (end of branch). Look at the facts and sources
